scenes.title: 1998 Pittsburgh Tabletop: Vertical Screen Hiding the Real Left Hand While Twin Paintbrushes Stroke the Visible Rubber Hand in Sync
scenes.era: 1998, University of Pittsburgh / Carnegie Mellon cognitive neuroscience lab

layout.description: Sunlit high-key psychology laboratory table fitted with a clean vertical matte-white wooden partition screen: to the left of the partition sits the participant's real left hand (visible to our camera angle, hidden from the participant's eyes); in front of the participant's chest rests a realistic beige-matte prosthetic left hand draped from a cloth cuff, with an under-table centimeter ruler strip measuring blindfolded pointing drift.

positions.who: Experimenter mannequin (in 1998 crisp collared shirt and lab coat)
positions.where: seated across the table holding two identical camel-hair paintbrushes — stroking the index knuckle of the visible prosthetic hand and the hidden real hand in exact unison
gazing intently at the visible prosthetic left hand while their real left hand rests calmly behind the vertical partition screen

props.name: vertical tabletop occlusion partition & realistic prosthetic left hand
props.period_detail: hides the real left hand from the subject's sight while positioning the fake hand in anatomically natural alignment

props.name: matched pair of fine camel-hair paintbrushes
props.period_detail: delivers identical synchronous strokes (vs 500-ms asynchronous control)
props.physical_behavior: the two-dollar tool that rewrites body boundaries

props.name: under-table centimeter Proprioceptive Drift ruler
props.period_detail: measures blindfolded right-hand pointing shifting centimeters toward the prosthetic hand
props.physical_behavior: objective physical readout of recalibrated body sense

actions.verb_sequence: strokes both the hidden real hand and visible prosthetic hand in crisp synchrony for 60 seconds -> asks blindfolded Participant to slide right index finger under the table to point at their left hand -> finger lands centimeters shifted toward the prosthetic hand

reactions.reaction: opens eyes in astonishment at where their pointing finger landed on the centimeter ruler
contrasts synchronous drift against flat zero-drift on asynchronous strokes

scenes.wardrobe: Late-1990s academic attire: crisp white lab coat over button-down shirt; crew-neck cotton sweater.
scenes.lighting: Clean high-key studio daylight showing both sides of the partition clearly to the viewer.
scenes.recognition_hook: Hide your real hand behind a board, stroke a fake rubber hand in sync for sixty seconds, and your brain relocates where your own fingers live.

key_visual.description: a psychology table divided by a vertical partition where an experimenter uses two matching paintbrushes to stroke a participant's hidden real hand and a visible prosthetic hand in unison above a centimeter drift ruler

scenes.title: Flinching From a Threat to Dead Rubber (Ehrsson 2007)

layout.description: Same partition table wired with clean finger skin-conductance sensors on the participant's right hand.

positions.where: after 60s synchronous brushing, Experimenter brings a blunt reflex hammer briskly toward the fake hand -> Participant gasps and pulls their REAL hidden hand back as the sweat trace spikes!

props.name: palmar skin-conductance trace monitor & reflex tester
props.period_detail: proves visceral autonomic alarm treats the fake hand as living self

actions.verb_sequence: moves reflex hammer toward fake fingers -> skin-conductance line jumps sharply and hidden real hand retracts

reactions.reaction: laughs nervously realizing the fake hand couldn't possibly hurt

scenes.recognition_hook: Swing a reflex tester toward a lifeless rubber glove after synchronous brushing, and your real sweat glands fire like you're in danger.

scenes.title: Breaking the Spell: Out-of-Sync Strokes & Twisted Posture

layout.description: Clean tabletop showing 500-ms alternating brush strokes and a wooden block substitute.

positions.where: shaking head calmly with zero ownership and zero pointing drift when strokes alternate out of sync

props.name: asynchronous timing metronome & wooden block control
props.period_detail: proves both temporal synchrony AND human hand geometry are required

actions.verb_sequence: strokes left-then-right 500 ms apart -> Participant points accurately straight to real hidden hand

reactions.reaction: marks zero drift on control chart

scenes.recognition_hook: Delay one paintbrush by half a second — or swap the hand for a block of wood — and the illusion vanishes completely.

scenes.title: Bionic Prosthetics That Feel Like 'MY Hand' Again

layout.description: Sunlit clinical studio where an upper-limb amputee wears a sleek white articulated bionic hand wired to sensory nerve feedback.

positions.where: touching a porcelain cup and feeling instantaneous synchronous touch + sight, smiling as the prosthetic feels like part of their own body rather than a heavy tool

props.name: touch-feedback bionic hand & porcelain cup
props.period_detail: applies synchronous sight + touch to restore natural embodiment

actions.verb_sequence: grasps cup smoothly with zero visual strain as tactile feedback fires in sync

scenes.wardrobe: Modern clinic jacket and smart-casual tee.
scenes.recognition_hook: The same 60-second rule that tricked volunteers into owning rubber now helps bionic hands feel genuinely alive to amputees.
